transcript.text: This is Swift, an automated flood assistant working with local emergency services. Am I speaking with someone at 986 Creekhaven Drive?
Yeah, this is me at 986 Creekhaven Drive—just me and two others, no one’s stuck inside, and I’ve got a boat handy if we need to get out, no truck though.
Got it, you’re at 986 Creekhaven Drive with two others. How many people are at the home right now, including anyone who can't come to the phone?
Yeah, just the three of us here at 986 Creekhaven Drive, no one’s stuck inside or anything—everyone’s accounted for, and we’re all good to go.

Thanks for confirming everyone is accounted for and ready to go. Is there anyone there who can't leave on their own, for example someone who uses a wheelchair, needs oxygen, or is bedbound? If it's a wheelchair, does it have a motor?
No one here can’t leave on their own, and no wheelchairs or oxygen needs—just three of us, all good to go, and we’ve got a boat ready if needed.
Understood, no one here can’t leave on their own. Is there water inside the home right now?
No water inside at all, just us three folks hanging tight, and yeah, we’ve got a boat handy if you’re coming—no truck though, sorry.
Thanks for the update, staying safe is key. If neighbors need a ride out, do you have a high-clearance truck, a boat, or free seats in a vehicle?
Yeah, I’m good here, no water inside, and I’ve got a boat handy if anyone needs to get out—just say the word, 986 Creekhaven Drive!
Thanks for offering your boat, 986 Creekhaven Drive. Let me read that back: 3 people; no water inside yet; you can help with a boat. Is that right?
Yeah, that’s right—three people here, no water in yet, and I’ve got a boat ready to go, no problem!

Got it, three people, no water in, boat ready. I've recorded that you may be able to help neighbors. A dispatcher may contact you. Only go out if it's safe for you, and never drive into water you can't see the bottom of. Goodbye.
